domain: public procurement / tender-process outcome prediction (Kenya national + county governments)
prediction_question: At the tender-publication instant of a Kenyan public procurement process published on the Public Procurement Information Portal (PPIP), using only at-publication attributes (buyer entity, procurement method, main procurement category, award criteria, title text, tender-period dates), predict whether the process will end with at least one published contract award within a censoring window after the tender period closes, versus no award ever published (a mixture of cancellation, retender and non-publication that the portal does not distinguish - tender.status is null on 6,727/6,727 sampled 2018 records). A useful prediction would support PPRA's own compliance-monitoring question - which published tenders silently die - and citizen-oversight prioritisation. The licence veto recorded below was established before any task probing; no novelty claim is made in either direction.
prediction_time: The tender-publication instant (release 'date' / tender first appearing in PPIP); only forward evidence of the outcome window follows it. Not further specified because the lead was closed at the licence gate.
target_definition: Binary: >=1 published award on the process within the censoring window vs none. Label source column: awards array of the OCDS record (excludable by construction). Right-censoring (processes whose window has not closed) excluded by eligibility cutoff. Measured on the OCP mirror's 2018 year-file: 2,074/6,727 records (30.8%) carry >=1 award; 4,653 carry none. tender.status is null throughout, so no explicit cancelled status exists in this publication.

sources.name: Public Procurement Information Portal (PPIP) - PPRA Open Contracting Data Standard publication
sources.api: OCDS bulk endpoint https://tenders.go.ke/api/ocds/tenders?fy=<financial-year> - live but aggressively rate-limited: two anonymous GETs on 2026-11-07 (one bare, one after 45 s) both returned HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests' (Laravel rate-limiter page, 6,619 bytes). The Open Contracting Partnership mirror serves the same records anonymously: https://data.open-contracting.org/en/publication/147 (full.jsonl.gz 43 MB; per-year files; 2018.jsonl.gz 863,775 bytes fetched in 0.39 s). OCP registry counts (its own monthly mirror of PPRA, last retrieved 2026-11-03): 262,961 tenders, 109,607 awards, 80,309 suppliers, 818,997 parties, Jul 2018 - Oct 2026, daily update frequency. OCP data-quality review (Dec 2024): awards/contracts empty arrays common, extreme outliers in awards/value/amount, no organisational identifier schemes, tenderers/items/milestones/amendments counts all zero. Registry's own 'License' field: empty.

license_evidence: Publisher instrument 1 (2026-11-07, read through the supported browser because the portal is a JS app): PPIP footer on the SPA shell and on https://tenders.go.ke/ocds reads 'Public Procurement Information Portal © 2026 All Rights Reserved | Powered by @iLabAfrica, Strathmore'. Bare copyright, no reuse or redistribution grant anywhere on the app surface.

Publisher instrument 2 (2026-11-07, browser): PPIP support center https://tenders.go.ke/helpdesk/ footer reads 'Copyright © 2026 PPRA. All rights reserved'. Its FAQ/knowledgebase sections list support topics only; no terms-of-use or data-licence page is linked from the SPA, the /ocds page or the helpdesk.

Publisher instrument 3 (2026-11-07, curl): the Authority's own site ppra.go.ke exposes no data-licence or terms-of-use page; its 'Licensing' menu item (https://ppra.go.ke/licensing/) is supplier/procurement licensing (licencees, permits, authorizations), not a data licence; /terms-conditions/ and /disclaimer/ return WordPress 404s.

Third-party corroboration (2026-11-07): the Open Contracting Partnership's data registry page for publication 147 records 'License: -' (empty) - OCP, which reviews this publication, could not find a licence either.

Executive Order No. 2 of 2018 and Constitution of Kenya Article 227 mandate that procuring entities DISCLOSE procurement information through the portal. An obligation to publish is not a grant of reuse or redistribution rights; Kenyan government works carry copyright under the Copyright Act (no PSI public-domain rule). The mandate is therefore not an open-data licence, and this is recorded so a future session does not mistake it for one.
split_strategy: Not reached (licence veto). For scale planning on any reopen: OCP mirror year-files 2018 (<1 MB) through 2024 (11 MB gz) suggest tens of thousands of contracting processes per year (6,727 in 2018), so temporal split capacity would likely be measurable; the outcome base rate measured on 2018 is 30.8% with-award, but it is one year of a drift-prone publication and no window counts were computed.

measurements.pip_api_rate_limited_2026_11_07: GET https://tenders.go.ke/api/ocds/tenders?fy=2026-2027 twice (second attempt after 45 s): both HTTP 429, 6,619-byte Laravel 'Too Many Requests' page. Endpoint exists and answers; throttled from the coordinator IP, not absent.
measurements.ocp_mirror_sample_2018_2026_11_07: data.open-contracting.org publication 147 year-file 2018.jsonl.gz: HTTP 200, 863,775 bytes, 0.39 s. Parsed 6,727 release records: top-level keys buyer/date/id/initiationType/language/ocid/parties/tag/tender; tender keys awardCriteria/id/mainProcurementCategory/procurementMethod/tenderPeriod/title; tender.status null on 6,727/6,727; >=1 award on 2,074 (30.8%); procurementMethod open 6,103 / selective 342 / direct 282; buyer names populated (sample: 'Kenya Ordnance factories corporation'). Probe retained at candidates/ke-ppra-ppip-procurement-outcome/probe_ocds_sample.py.
measurements.portal_reachability_2026_11_07: https://tenders.go.ke/ HTTP 200 in 1.17 s (curl) and rendered in the supported browser (SPA title 'PPIP'); /ocds and /helpdesk/ render. Access is not the blocker.

jurisdiction.publisher: Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) - Public Procurement Information Portal, tenders.go.ke

rejection_reason: Licence veto (class C, closed under the 2026-10-21 standing policy). The strongest task-shaped unit-level Kenyan source found to date - OCDS contracting processes for all national and county buyers, July 2018 to present, daily updates, anonymous bulk access via the OCP mirror and a live (rate-limited) publisher API - is published under bare copyright: '© 2026 All Rights Reserved' on the portal footer and 'Copyright © 2026 PPRA. All rights reserved' on the PPRA support center, with no reuse/redistribution grant on any publisher instrument (SPA, /ocds page, helpdesk, ppra.go.ke), while the OCP registry's own licence field is empty. The disclosure mandate (Executive Order No. 2 of 2018) is not a licence. This mirrors the CBK 2026-10-30 closure and completes the same finding for Kenya's second major open-data-adjacent channel. No task probing, schema census or split counting was done past this gate; novelty is neither claimed nor denied.
review: This was the Africa tick's most promising new lead before the licence gate: unit-level, ongoing, decision-relevant, cleanly standardised (OCDS), with a stateable publication instant and a target observable after it. Killed at the cheapest gate, before construction spend, exactly as the triage policy intends. The pattern now recorded twice in Kenya (CBK auction data, PPIP procurement data) is that Kenyan government data instruments default to bare 'All rights reserved' copyright even where an executive order mandates disclosure; future Kenya-focused sessions should read the footer FIRST and budget no more than a channel sweep before closing.
next_action: Closed 2026-11-07. Reopen ONLY if: (a) PPRA/PPIP states an open licence or terms permitting redistribution of derived rows on a publisher instrument (re-check the SPA footer, /ocds page, helpdesk and ppra.go.ke; the 2026-11-07 channel list is in license_evidence and need not be re-derived); (b) the operator records an explicit candidate-specific risk acceptance per skills/dataset-discovery/references/licence-posture.md - one candidate, never extendable to sibling Kenyan sources; or (c) the operator authorises a written licence enquiry (the standing default is no unsolicited permission email). If reopened, the first probes are: publisher-side (non-mirror) per-year census to confirm the OCP counts; award-publication-lag measurement from tender-period end to award date (right-censoring margin); per-year with-award base rate drift (2018 measured at 30.8% via the mirror); then novelty search against OCDS-based procurement prediction literature (Ukraine ProZorro et al.) before any construction.
